message.content: I'll record a claim about full-domain exactness of the AES SubBytes Triton kernel, then probe it exhaustively (all 256 byte values plus varied lengths and storage offsets).

function.arguments: {"rationale": "The kernel uses a nonstandard tower-field decomposition (bits via `_basis` with the `_TO_TOWER`/`_FROM_TOWER` matrices, GF(16) multiplication, norm-based inversion). Any error in those constants or in the bit-mapping order would produce wrong S-box entries that only an exhaustive check over all 256 byte values would reveal. The contract demands exact values with zero tolerance over the full domain (all 256 byte values, lengths 1..131072, nonzero storage offsets allowed).", "scope": "in_scope", "scope_evidence": [{"source": "problem.txt", "summary": "'Every byte value from 0 through 255 is legal, in every arrangement' and 'the exact specified value at every position. There is no numerical tolerance.' Also 'Contiguous views with nonzero storage offsets are also legal' and lengths 1 through 131072 are legal."}], "scope_rationale": "The contract requires exact AES SubBytes output for every byte value 0..255, every legal length 1..131072, and contiguous views with nonzero storage offsets, with no numerical tolerance. A wrong S-box value on any input in that domain violates the contract.", "statement": "The kernel's `run` produces the exact AES SubBytes (FIPS 197 5.1.1) output for every input byte value 0..255, and for all contract-legal input configurations (all lengths 1..131072 including non-multiples of the 256 block size, and contiguous views with nonzero storage offsets), and preserves input storage without sharing it with the output."}
function.name: record_claim
